evidence: src/application/inventory-service.ts: InventoryService has ProductRepository injected through the constructor; listStock and getStock return ProductSnapshot through product.toSnapshot()

src/application/order-service.ts: OrderService has OrderRepository, ProductRepository, IdGenerator and Clock injected through the constructor; all public methods return OrderSnapshot through toSnapshot()
src/application/order-service.ts placeOrder: leaves the stock rules to the domain through product.canReserve, product.reserve and assertPositiveInteger
src/application/order-service.ts changeState/advance/cancel: leave the state machine to the domain through order.transitionTo and order.nextState

Minor duplication: the product lookup that throws NotFoundError(`Product ${id} not found`) appears in InventoryService.getStock, in OrderService.requireProduct, and written out inside OrderService.placeOrder
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files serve one concern: application services that coordinate domain objects for order and inventory use cases. They use the same abstractions in the same way. Each receives its domain repository ports (ProductRepository, OrderRepository, Clock, IdGenerator) through the constructor, returns snapshots through toSnapshot(), and reports failures with domain errors. The business rules stay in the domain and are not re-implemented here: availability is checked with Product.canReserve, stock moves through reserve, ship and release, quantities are validated with assertPositiveInteger, and order transitions go through Order.transitionTo and nextState. One small duplication exists: the "find the product by id or throw NotFoundError" lookup appears in InventoryService.getStock, in OrderService.requireProduct, and again written out inside OrderService.placeOrder instead of calling requireProduct. This is a repeated lookup pattern, not a duplicated business rule or invariant, so it does not reach the fail threshold. Consolidating it would be a small improvement.
